implementation.name: original-v1-activation-clipping
implementation.scope: Original ResNet-50 layer histogram; bar heights are the figure's TikZ digitization (adapted from wu2020integer), so clipped shares are illustrative. Non-negative activations on the chapter's affine UINT8 grid (alpha = 0, s = beta/255, z = 0). Thresholds on 0.1 bin edges; no KL/MSE/accuracy optimum; motion is not time.
implementation.question: How much do I clip, and how coarse is the step?

purpose: Move one clipping threshold across the printed bars: watch the UINT8 step and its rounding bound shrink while tail bars, then bulk bars, become clipped and the clipped share and largest clipped-value error grow.

storyboard.label: The printed histogram
storyboard.description: Original bars, red tail, and green candidate line at 1.1; no threshold applied, empty code ruler.

storyboard.label: Max method: beta at the last occupied bin, 2.1
Lower beta to 1.6
storyboard.description: Five tail bars clipped (1.4% of plotted mass); s = 0.00627; a clipped value can be off by up to 0.5.

storyboard.label: Lower beta to the printed candidate, 1.1
storyboard.description: The 1.1-1.2 bulk bar and all nine red bars clipped (6.4%); s = 0.00431; clipped-value error up to 1.0.

storyboard.label: Push beta into the bulk, 0.5
storyboard.description: Sixteen bars clipped (36.3%); s = 0.00196; clipping now truncates the dense bulk.

storyboard.label: Compare the two error terms
storyboard.description: Back at 1.1 with a reader-controlled threshold on the bin edges 0.1-2.5 and a table of the visited thresholds; framed as the trade-off calibration methods resolve differently, not an accuracy prediction.

guard: Exact TikZ bar table and SVG geometry; the default state is the printed figure and the added threshold starts at the printed 1.1 in the final state. Clipped share is a share of digitized relative-frequency bars, labeled illustrative; no percentile rank, KL, MSE, or accuracy claim. Unsigned UINT8 grid stated explicitly (fig-calibration-ranges uses signed INT8). Readout shows committed values only; all values come from calc.py.
